docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
maxodiff intends to support the decision that is commonly encountered in rare-disease diagnostics: Which diagnostic test should be performed next to provide the greatest amount of information that could improve the accuracy of the differential diagnosis?

Given a patient's phenotypic features (as HPO terms) and a differential diagnosis, maxodiff estimates, for each candidate diagnostic procedure from the Medical Action Ontology (MAxO), how much the ranking of the differential diagnosis is expected to change if the procedure is performed. Procedures that are likely to reveal new, discriminating findings are ranked highest.

Maxodiff is implemented as a Java application that can be run as a stand-alone command line app, run as an HTML server, or can be accessed from Symptom annotation made simple (SAMS), a database and phenotyping tool.

docs.title: Inputs and Outputs
docs.text: Input Output A GA4GH phenopacket with the patient's observed and excluded HPO terms A list of MAxO procedures, ordered by their expected effect on the differential diagnosis The number of top-ranked diseases to consider and the number of simulation repetitions For each procedure, which diseases are expected to move up or down, and by how much

docs.title: Ways to run maxodiff
docs.text: Web server Command line Best for Trying it out on a single patient; integration in other tools such as SAMS Batch analyses, scripting, offline use Output Interactive page, or JSON Self-contained HTML file Documentation Server setup, Web server output Setup, Command line app

docs.title: JSON API
docs.text:
Other programs can use maxodiff over HTTP. The server accepts a phenopacket as JSON and returns the results as JSON. This is the interface that SAMS uses.

Pilot phase

The JSON format is in a pilot stage. We are actively seeking feedback to refine the data structure.

Start the server first. The examples assume that it runs on localhost:8080.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Purpose POST /api/analyze Rank diagnostic procedures for a patient POST /api/modality?targetDiseaseId=<id> Rank procedures with respect to one target disease

Both endpoints expect the phenopacket as the body of the request, with the header Content-Type: application/json. The phenopacket must have an id.

docs.title: Analyze a patient
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/analyze \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @docs/examples/example-phenopacket.json \
  -o response.json

The example uses example-phenopacket.json. The analysis takes about 30 seconds.

The analysis uses the top 20 diseases and 80 repetitions. These values cannot be changed through the API.

docs.title: Structure of the response
docs.text:
The response is one JSON object:

Field Meaning ppktId The id of the phenopacket nDiseases Number of diseases that were analyzed (20) nRepetitions Number of simulations per procedure (80) observedHpoTerms HPO terms that are observed in the patient excludedHpoTerms HPO terms that are excluded in the patient resultList One entry per MAxO procedure, sorted by maxoScore, highest first

Every entry of resultList describes one procedure:

Field Meaning maxoTerm The MAxO procedure maxoScore The score (ΔScore): how much the procedure is expected to change the ranking. See Reading the results. rankedOmimTermList The analyzed diseases. averageRank is the average rank of the disease over all simulations (rank 1 is the best). hpoTermIds HPO terms that the procedure could reveal. count is the number of simulations in which the term was drawn. frequencies For each pair of disease and revealable HPO term: frequency, the frequency of the term in patients with the disease, and mica, the information content of the term for that disease

Terms are given by their identifier only, for example {"tid": "MAXO:0000703"}. Labels are not part of the response.

Abridged example (shortened with ..., so it is not valid JSON):

{
  "ppktId": "PMID_36322151_KDM2B_23",
  "nDiseases": 20,
  "nRepetitions": 80,
  "observedHpoTerms": [ { "tid": "HP:0000122" }, { "tid": "HP:0001631" }, ... ],
  "excludedHpoTerms": [ { "tid": "HP:0011255" }, ... ],
  "resultList": [
    {
      "maxoTerm": { "tid": "MAXO:0000703" },
      "maxoScore": 12.343383583865394,
      "rankedOmimTermList": [
        { "tid": "OMIM:621220", "averageRank": 1.9 },
        { "tid": "OMIM:615829", "averageRank": 4.0125 },
        ...
      ],
      "hpoTermIds": [
        { "tid": "HP:0000540", "count": 20 },
        { "tid": "HP:0000565", "count": 17 },
        ...
      ],
      "frequencies": [
        { "diseaseId": "OMIM:621570", "hpoId": "HP:0000540", "frequency": 0.25, "mica": 3.6826675 },
        ...
      ]
    },
    ...
  ]
}

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• The initial rank is not in the response. rankedOmimTermList lists the diseases in the order of the initial differential diagnosis. The position in the list (starting at 1) is the initial rank. The change of a disease is averageRank minus its position. The same order is used in every entry.
  • All procedures are returned, also those with score 0. In the example response, 186 of 312 procedures have a score of 0. They cannot change the ranking. Skip them in your program.
  • The response can be large (about 0.5 MB in the example).

docs.title: Best procedures for one disease
docs.text:
If you suspect one disease, ask for the procedures that help most to confirm or exclude it:

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/api/modality?targetDiseaseId=OMIM:157700" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @docs/examples/example-phenopacket.json

The target disease id is required and can be an OMIM id (substitute any OMIM id). The response is a list, sorted by maxoScore, highest first:

[
  {
    "targetDisease": { "tid": "OMIM:157700" },
    "maxoTerm": { "tid": "MAXO:0035050" },
    "nMaxoPhenotypes": 1,
    "totalIC": 9.061724347647399,
    "maxoScore": 8.499235179380303
  },
  {
    "targetDisease": { "tid": "OMIM:157700" },
    "maxoTerm": { "tid": "MAXO:0000706" },
    "nMaxoPhenotypes": 2,
    "totalIC": 7.263296516746243,
    "maxoScore": 16.172687354838573
  }
]
Field Meaning targetDisease The disease that you asked for maxoTerm The MAxO procedure nMaxoPhenotypes Number of phenotypes of the target disease that the procedure can reveal totalIC Sum of the information content of those phenotypes maxoScore The score of the procedure for the target disease

The values in the example are illustrative.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status Meaning 200 The analysis was done. 400 The request has no phenopacket or the phenopacket has no id.

You can also get the JSON through the web page: choose JSON as the output.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
The command-line tool runs maxodiff on one phenopacket and writes the results to a file. Use it for batch analyses, scripting, or if you do not want to run a server.

Before you start

You need Java 21 or newer, the maxodiff JAR file, and the downloaded data files. See Installation.

All examples assume that you run them from the folder that contains the JAR file and the data folder.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Run the JAR without arguments to see the list of commands:

java -jar maxodiff-cli.jar
Command Short Purpose download D Download the HPO and MAxO data files and prepare them for analysis analyze A Analyze one phenopacket (the main command) modality M Find the best diagnostic procedures for one named target disease precompute-resnik Recompute the term similarity file from the downloaded data benchmarking BX Evaluate maxodiff on many phenopackets (for developers)

Add -h to any command for its full list of options, for example java -jar maxodiff-cli.jar analyze -h. Use -V to print the version.

docs.title: Download the data
docs.text:
java -jar maxodiff-cli.jar download

This downloads hp.json, phenotype.hpoa, maxo.json, and the MAxO diagnostic annotations into a data folder, and then computes the term similarity file data/term-pair-similarity.ser (the file is about 100 MB and takes a few minutes to compute).

Option Meaning -d, --data Folder for the data files (default: data) -w, --overwrite Replace files that were downloaded earlier

HPO and MAxO are updated several times a year. To update your data, run the command again with -w.

docs.title: Analyze one phenopacket
docs.text:
java -jar maxodiff-cli.jar analyze -p patient.json

This runs the analysis with default settings and writes an HTML file in the current folder. A progress bar shows how far the analysis is.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning -p, --phenopacket (required) Path to the phenopacket JSON file -n, --nDiseases 20 Number of top-ranked diseases that are analyzed -nr, --nRepetitions 80 Number of simulations per procedure. More repetitions give more stable results and take longer. -t, --nThreads smaller of 4 and the number of CPU cores Number of threads -j, --json off Write JSON instead of HTML -m, --maxoData data Folder with the downloaded data files -f, --outFilename Name of the output file (the suffix .html or .json is added if missing) -O, --outputDirectory current folder Folder for the output file -v More log output; repeat for more detail (-vv)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Use 40 diseases and 100 repetitions:

java -jar maxodiff-cli.jar analyze -p patient.json -n 40 -nr 100

Write JSON:

java -jar maxodiff-cli.jar analyze -p patient.json -j

Choose the name and the folder of the output file:

java -jar maxodiff-cli.jar analyze -p patient.json -O results -f patient1

This writes results/patient1.html.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Without -f, the file is written to the current folder and named after the sample id of the phenopacket:

<sample id>_<nDiseases>_<nRepetitions>_maxodiff_results.html

The HTML file is self-contained. You can open it in a browser without internet access and send it to colleagues. Reading the results explains the page. The JSON file contains all procedures with a score greater than zero, with the full details.

docs.title: Running time
docs.text: The running time grows with the number of repetitions and diseases and falls with more threads. With the defaults, an analysis takes about a minute on a laptop. Do not set the number of threads higher than the number of CPU cores of your machine.

docs.title: Best procedures for a target disease
docs.text:
If you already suspect one disease, modality ranks procedures with respect to that disease:

java -jar maxodiff-cli.jar modality -p patient.json --targetDisease OMIM:157700 -j
Option Meaning -p, --phenopacket Phenopacket file (required) --targetDisease Identifier of the target disease, for example OMIM:157700 (required). The prefix must be OMIM, ORPHA, or DECIPHER. -j, --json Write the results to a JSON file named <sample id>_maxodiff_modalities.json -O, --outputDirectory Folder for the JSON file -t, --nThreads Number of threads

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Could not find phenopacket file The path after -p is wrong. Check it and the current folder. The program stalls for a long time at Loading Maxodiff resources, then fails Java has not enough memory. Allow more with -Xmx, for example java -Xmx8g -jar maxodiff-cli.jar analyze -p patient.json. Connection refused or a connection timeout during download You may be behind a proxy. Pass the proxy to Java: java -Dhttps.proxyHost=<host> -Dhttps.proxyPort=<port> -jar maxodiff-cli.jar download. HPO file does not exist You have not downloaded the data yet, or you run the command from a different folder. Run download first or point to the files with --hpo and --hpoa.

docs.text:

docs.title: What is a differential diagnosis?
docs.text:
The process of differential diagnosis aims to identify the cause of a condition by evaluating the patient's history, physical examination findings, and in many cases laboratory data or imaging. The result of this process can be conceptualized as a ranked list of candidate diagnoses. The goal is to find the correct diagnosis so that clinical management can be planned optimally.

Every further test or examination can change this list: a new finding makes some diagnoses more likely and others less likely. An assumption of our method, and one that is also taught to medical students, is that a test whose outcome does not change clinical management is useless. Computationally, we model this by prioritizing tests that are expected to change the list the most.

docs.title: HPO and MAxO
docs.text:
The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) provides a semantically unified framework of knowledge on diseases, genes, and phenotypes. It is widely used to support phenotype-driven differential diagnosis and variant prioritization in medical genetics and other fields.

The Medical Action Ontology (MAxO) organizes medical procedures, therapies, and interventions, collectively called medical actions. These include pharmaceutical treatment, surgery, behavioral and cognitive interventions, and diagnostic procedures. The MAxO project also provides annotations that link diagnostic procedures (MAxO terms) to the clinical findings (HPO terms) that they can reveal.

Example. One such annotation states that the HPO term Corneal crystals is observable through slit-lamp examination (MAXO:0000973).

Corneal crystals are tiny crystalline deposits in the cornea that appear as shiny, refractile spots on slit-lamp examination. Several diseases can manifest with them, including Cystinosis and Bietti crystalline dystrophy. Finding corneal crystals would make these diseases rank higher in the differential and lower the rank of diseases that are not characterized by corneal crystals.

docs.title: How does maxodiff work?
docs.text:
For a given patient, maxodiff proceeds as follows:

  1. Initial ranking. The patient's observed and excluded HPO terms are used to rank diseases with the Phenomizer algorithm. The top-ranked diseases are the differential diagnosis that maxodiff will try to improve.
  2. Candidate procedures. For every MAxO procedure, maxodiff collects the HPO terms that the procedure can reveal and that are not already part of the patient's description.
  3. Simulating the result of a procedure. We do not know what a procedure will find in this patient, so maxodiff simulates it. It draws a plausible set of new HPO terms from the revealable terms. Terms that occur in highly ranked candidate diseases are drawn more often than terms that occur only in lower ranked ones, because the top candidates are more likely to be the correct diagnosis.
  4. Re-ranking. The drawn terms are added to the patient's description and the diseases are ranked again.
  5. Repetition. Steps 3 and 4 are repeated many times (the number of repetitions is a parameter), each time starting from the original patient. For each disease, maxodiff records its average rank across repetitions.
  6. Comparison. The average rank of each disease is compared with its initial rank. Procedures that move the diseases of the differential diagnosis apart, so that they can be told from each other, are ranked highest.

Because the procedure's result is simulated by random sampling, repeated runs give slightly different numbers. Using more repetitions makes the results more stable at the cost of a longer running time.

See Reading the results for how these numbers are displayed.

docs.title: GA4GH Phenopackets
docs.text:
The input for maxodiff is a Global Alliance for Genomics and Health (GA4GH) phenopacket. The Phenopacket Schema is a standard for sharing disease and phenotype information about an individual person or biosample (see Jacobsen et al., 2022). Each phenopacket describes one individual and can include phenotypic descriptions, measurements, genetic information, diagnoses, and treatments.

maxodiff uses the observed and excluded HPO terms of the phenopacket. To run the web version, only a phenopacket is required. The command-line version needs a little more setup.

To try the software, you can download phenopackets from Phenopacket Store (see also Danis et al., 2025), which currently provides over 10,000 phenopackets.

The following tools can help to convert existing data to phenopacket format:

  • SAMS (Symptom annotation made simple): a database and phenotyping tool for precision medicine that can create phenopackets.
  • phenopacket-tools: Java library and command-line application (see also Danis et al., 2023).
  • phenopackets: Python library.
  • phenopacket-schema: Java library.

docs.title: Profiling
docs.text:
echo PPKT="/path/to/phenopacket.json"
java -XX:StartFlightRecording=disk=true,dumponexit=true,filename=maxodiff_profile2.jfr,settings=profile \
     -jar maxodiff-cli/target/maxodiff-cli.jar \
     analyze -p $PPKT

docs.title: Using maxodiff in SAMS
docs.text:
Work in progress

The integration of maxodiff in SAMS (Symptom annotation made simple) is under development. This page will be completed when it is released.

SAMS is a database and phenotyping tool for precision medicine. It supports documenting a patient's clinical signs and symptoms with HPO terms and can export them as a phenopacket. The planned integration will let you send a patient from SAMS to maxodiff and see which diagnostic procedures are expected to help most.

docs.title: Web server
docs.text: The maxodiff web server provides a web page for analyzing a phenopacket and a JSON API for other programs such as SAMS. You can run it on your own machine, or in a Docker container.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  • Java 21 or newer.
  • The JAR file maxodiff-html.jar (see Installation).
  • The data files, created by the download command of the command-line tool. The server expects a folder named data in the folder where you start it.
  • About 8 GB of memory for the server.

docs.title: Run the server locally
docs.text:
java -Xmx8g -jar maxodiff-html.jar

Loading the data takes about 20 seconds. When the server is ready, open http://localhost:8080/maxodiff in your browser.

Useful settings (add them after the JAR file name):

Setting Meaning Default --server.port=9090 Port of the server 8080 --maxodiff.data-directory=/path/to/data Folder with the data files data

If Java reports a heap space error or the server stalls at Loading Maxodiff resources, give Java more memory, for example -Xmx12g.

docs.title: Use the web page
docs.text:
1. Choose a phenopacket file in the Sample Input box. The observed and excluded HPO terms are displayed.
  2. Choose the number of diseases (20 or 40) and the number of repetitions (20 to 100).
  3. Choose the output: HTML shows the results page, JSON returns the raw data.
  4. Click Run maxodiff.

The analysis takes between 30 seconds and a few minutes, depending on the number of repetitions and HPO terms.

If a value is outside the allowed range, the page does not run the analysis. It explains in plain language what is wrong and what you can do.

docs.title: Threads and concurrent requests
docs.text:
The analysis needs a lot of CPU time. The server therefore uses one pool of analysis threads for the whole application, no matter how many users are connected:

  • Pool size: the larger of 2 and 10% of the available processors. In a Docker container, the CPU limit of the container counts.
  • Concurrent analyses: at most maxodiff.max-concurrent-analyses analyses run at the same time. Further requests wait for up to maxodiff.admission-wait-seconds. If no slot becomes free in that time, the server answers with HTTP 503 (server busy), and the client should try again later.
Property Default Meaning maxodiff.max-concurrent-analyses 2 Analyses that may run at once maxodiff.admission-wait-seconds 60 How long a request waits for a free slot before it gets a 503

Set them on the command line:

java -jar maxodiff-html.jar --maxodiff.max-concurrent-analyses=3 --maxodiff.admission-wait-seconds=120

Or with environment variables, which is easier in Docker or a service:

export MAXODIFF_MAX_CONCURRENT_ANALYSES=3
export MAXODIFF_ADMISSION_WAIT_SECONDS=120
java -jar maxodiff-html.jar

The command-line tool is separate. It has its own pool with at most 4 threads, which you can change with -t (see Command line).

docs.title: Prepare the data
docs.text:
The server image contains the data files. Create them before you build the image, from the root folder of the project:

./mvnw clean package
java -jar maxodiff-cli/target/maxodiff-cli.jar download

docs.title: Build the image
docs.text:
docker build -f maxodiff-html/Dockerfile -t maxodiff-html:latest .

The image is built from the sources, so you do not need Java or Maven on your machine, only Docker. If Docker runs out of memory during the build, increase the memory in the Docker settings (8 GB is a good start).

Behind a proxy, pass the proxy to the build:

docker build -f maxodiff-html/Dockerfile -t maxodiff-html:latest \
  --build-arg http_proxy=<proxy>:<port> --build-arg https_proxy=<proxy>:<port> \
  --build-arg MAVEN_OPTS="-Dhttp.proxyHost=<proxy> -Dhttp.proxyPort=<port> -Dhttps.proxyHost=<proxy> -Dhttps.proxyPort=<port>" .

docs.title: Start the container
docs.text:
docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -m 10g --name maxodiff-html-app maxodiff-html:latest
Option Meaning -d Run in the background. Leave it out to see the log in your terminal. -p 8080:8080 Make port 8080 of the container available on port 8080 of your machine -m 10g Memory limit of the container. It must be larger than the Java memory. --name maxodiff-html-app A name that makes it easy to stop the container and read its log

The server is then available at http://localhost:8080/maxodiff.

The Java memory is set to 8 GB by default. Change it with the environment variable JAVA_OPTS, and adapt -m accordingly:

docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -m 6g -e JAVA_OPTS="-Xms4g -Xmx4g" \
  --name maxodiff-html-app maxodiff-html:latest

Docker Desktop must have enough memory: choose at least 12 GB under Settings > Resources.

To use data files from a folder on your machine instead of the files in the image, mount it:

docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -m 10g -v "$(pwd)/data:/app/data" \
  --name maxodiff-html-app maxodiff-html:latest

docs.title: Everyday commands
docs.text: Task Command Show all containers, also stopped ones docker ps -a Read the log (first place to look after a failed start) docker logs maxodiff-html-app Stop the container docker stop maxodiff-html-app Remove the container docker rm maxodiff-html-app

docs.title: Rebuild after a change
docs.text:
docker rm -f maxodiff-html-app
docker rmi maxodiff-html:latest
docker build -f maxodiff-html/Dockerfile -t maxodiff-html:latest .
docker run -d -p 8080:8080 -m 10g --name maxodiff-html-app maxodiff-html:latest

docs.title: Run the command-line tool in Docker
docs.text:
A second image runs one analysis on the command line and exits. This is convenient for batch runs. It uses the JAR file that you built, so build the project first:

./mvnw clean package
java -jar maxodiff-cli/target/maxodiff-cli.jar download
docker build -f maxodiff-cli/Dockerfile -t maxodiff-cli:latest .

Run an analysis. The phenopacket is read from a folder that you mount, and the JSON result is written to another folder:

docker run --rm \
  -v "$(pwd)/docs/examples:/input" \
  -v "$(pwd)/results:/output" \
  -e PPKT=/input/example-phenopacket.json \
  -e OUT=/output \
  maxodiff-cli:latest
Variable Default Meaning PPKT (required) Path of the phenopacket inside the container OUT Folder for the result inside the container NDISEASES 20 Number of diseases NREPS 100 Number of repetitions

The container always writes JSON. The Java memory is set to 16 GB, so your Docker installation needs at least this much memory.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text:
Web server failed to start. Port 8080 was already in use.

Either use another port (--server.port=9090), or find the process that blocks the port:

lsof -i :8080

The output shows the process id (PID). Stop the process with kill <PID>. Use kill -9 <PID> only if it does not react.

docs.title: Out of memory
docs.text: If the server stalls at Loading Maxodiff resources and then fails, give Java more memory (-Xmx12g). In Docker, raise both JAVA_OPTS and the container limit -m.

docs.title: The server answers with 503
docs.text: The server is busy. Wait a moment and try again, or increase maxodiff.max-concurrent-analyses if your machine has more capacity.

docs.title: Connection refused during build or download
docs.text:
You may be behind a proxy. For Maven, set it before the build:

export MAVEN_OPTS="-Dhttp.proxyHost=<host> -Dhttp.proxyPort=<port> -Dhttps.proxyHost=<host> -Dhttps.proxyPort=<port>"
./mvnw clean package

For download, pass the proxy to Java:

java -Dhttps.proxyHost=<host> -Dhttps.proxyPort=<port> -jar maxodiff-cli/target/maxodiff-cli.jar download

docs.title: Setting up maxodiff
docs.text: MaxoDiff can be run from the command-line or as a Web application.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: maxodiff is a Java application. If you want to build maxodiff from source, then the build process described below requires Git and Java Development Kit (JDK) 21 or newer.

docs.title: Building from sources
docs.text:
To build maxodiff from sources, go the GitHub page of maxodiff, and clone or download the project, then build the executable JAR files from sources with Maven:

  git clone https://github.com/P2GX/maxodiff.git
  cd maxodiff
  ./mvnw clean package

We use the Maven Wrapper for building the sources, so installation of Maven prior to build is not required (but it is also possible to build as mvn clean package if desired).

docs.title: Download resources
docs.text:
We can download the resource files needed by maxodiff by running the download command of the CLI JAR:

java -jar maxodiff-cli/target/maxodiff-cli.jar download

The command will download the data files into data folder that will be created in the current working directory. See the command's documentation for more options.

Download frequency

The download command needs to be run everytime the user wants to update the HPO and MAxO files (which are updated roughly 5 times a year).

This command will automatically create the MICA dictionary with the latest downloaded files (see below).

docs.title: MICA dictionary
docs.text:
To run maxodiff with Phenomizer, we must first generate a file that contains the most informative common ancestors for pairs of HPO terms. maxodiff uses the Phenomizer algorithm to calculate the differential diagnosis; see the original publication for details: Clinical diagnostics in human genetics with semantic similarity searches in ontologies

To run this algorithm, we require the information content of the most informative common ancestor (MICA) for every pair of terms. It is more efficient to precalculate this using the following command. By default, the command will look for the input files hp.json and phenotype.hpoa in the datafolder, which is created by the download command.

The file will have been generated automatically by the download command. If you would like to regenerate the file, please enter the following command.

java -jar maxodiff-cli/target/maxodiff-cli.jar precompute-resnik
The optional --assume-annoated flag assumes that each term annotates at least one disease. This prevents IC=Infinity for the absent terms.

On a modern commodity laptop, this command will require a few minutes to complete. By default, the serialized output file will be created here. Currently, it occupies 100 Mb.

data/term-pair-similarity.ser

docs.title: Start Maxodiff web app
docs.text:
The web app can be started as:

java -jar maxodiff-html/target/maxodiff-html.jar

If a Java heap space error occurs, more memory can be allocated by adding VM options:

java -Xmx8g -jar maxodiff-html/target/maxodiff-html.jar

By default, the app will serve requests at http://localhost:8080/maxodiff.

docs.title: Connection refused
docs.text:
The error Connection refused might be a sign that you need to set proxy settings.

If ./mvnw clean package produces a connect exception, run export MAVEN_OPTS="-Dhttp.proxyHost=xxx -Dhttp.proxyPort=8080 -Dhttps.proxyHost=xxx -Dhttps.proxyPort=8080" (with your own proxy settings) in advance.

If java -jar maxodiff-cli/target/maxodiff-cli.jar downloadproduces a connect exception, try java -Dhttp.proxyHost=xxx -Dhttp.proxyPort=8080 -Dhttps.proxyHost=xxx -Dhttps.proxyPort=8080 -jar maxodiff-cli/target/maxodiff-cli.jar download (with your own proxy settings) instead.

docs.title: Running out of memory
docs.text: If java -jar maxodiff-html/target/maxodiff-html.jar stalls for a long time at Loading Maxodiff resources from xxx before failing, try giving java more heap space (in this example 12GB) with -Xmx12G, i.e. java -Xmx12G -jar maxodiff-html/target/maxodiff-html.jar.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text:
If you try to start the Webserver and see an error like this:

***************************
APPLICATION FAILED TO START
***************************

Description:

Web server failed to start. Port 8080 was already in use.

Then enter the following (adjust the port if needed)

lsof -i :8080
This will indicate the process id of the process () that is running on the port. Stop this process, e.g.,

docs.title: Understanding the results
docs.text: maxodiff produces the same results page whether you start it from SAMS, from the web server, or from the command line. This page explains how to read it.

docs.title: The idea in one paragraph
docs.text: You start with a ranked list of candidate diseases (the differential diagnosis), where rank 1 is the most likely disease. For each diagnostic procedure, maxodiff simulates what the procedure might find and checks how much the list would change. Procedures that are expected to change the list more are ranked higher, because they are more likely to help you tell the candidates apart. See Background for the method.

docs.title: Page overview
docs.text:
From top to bottom, the page shows:

  1. Summary of your input: the observed and excluded HPO terms, the number of diseases, and the number of simulations (repetitions).
  2. Detailed results for the 10 highest-scoring procedures.
  3. Other tests: a compact table for all remaining procedures.

If none of the procedures is expected to change the ranking, the page says so instead of showing results.

docs.title: The score (ΔScore)
docs.text:
Every procedure has one number, the ΔScore. It is used to order the page: the procedure with the largest ΔScore comes first.

In each simulation, maxodiff compares the new ranking with the initial ranking. For every disease it takes the number of rank positions that the disease moved and divides it by the disease's initial rank. The sum over all diseases is the score of that simulation, and the ΔScore is the average over all simulations.

Dividing by the initial rank means that a move near the top of the list counts more than the same move further down. Moving from rank 1 to rank 3 counts as 2, moving from rank 10 to rank 12 counts as 0.2.

Note

The ΔScore has no direction. It measures how much the list changes, not whether it gets better or worse. The direction for each disease is shown by the bars described below.

The ΔScore is a relative measure for ordering procedures for one patient. Do not compare ΔScore values between different patients or between runs with different numbers of diseases.

docs.title: A detailed result
docs.text: Each of the top 10 procedures has its own box.

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
• The MAxO term and its identifier (for example MAXO:0000973).
  • ΔScore, as described above.
  • N Diseases: the number of diseases that were ranked.
  • N Observed HPO Terms: the number of HPO terms that this procedure could reveal and that are not yet part of the patient's description.

docs.title: Average rank change per disease
docs.text:
The bar chart shows one row per disease, in the order of the initial differential diagnosis (the initial rank is shown before the disease name).

  • The middle line means "no change".
  • A bar to the left (blue) means that the disease moves up the list on average, to a smaller rank number: it becomes more likely.
  • A bar to the right (red) means that the disease moves down the list on average: it becomes less likely.
  • One unit is one rank position. The scale at the top shows the values. The numbers are averages over all simulations, so they need not be whole numbers. Hover over a bar to see the exact change, for example "Decline by 2.0".

What to look for

A good procedure moves some candidate diseases clearly up and others clearly down. If all bars are short, the procedure is not expected to help distinguish between the candidates.

docs.title: Which findings could the procedure reveal?
docs.text:
Under the chart, a table lists the HPO terms that the procedure could reveal (one column per term).

  • Observed in shows in how many of the simulations the term was drawn as a simulated finding. A darker cell means a more frequent term. Terms that are annotated to the highly ranked diseases are drawn more often. Hover over a cell to see how frequently the term is annotated to the candidate diseases.
  • Each row is a disease. The shading of a cell shows how strongly the term is associated with that disease, and the number is the information content of the most informative common ancestor (see below). An empty cell means that no such association was found.

docs.title: Other tests
docs.text:
Below the top 10, one table lists all other procedures with:

Column Meaning # Position of the procedure in the overall list MAxO term Name and identifier ΔScore The score described above HPO terms Number of HPO terms that the procedure could reveal Diseases moving up / down Number of diseases whose average rank gets smaller / larger

For these procedures, the full details are available in the JSON output.

docs.title: Why results can differ slightly between runs
docs.text: The result of a procedure is simulated by drawing HPO terms at random. Two runs for the same patient can therefore give slightly different numbers, especially with few simulations. If the order of the top procedures changes between runs, increase the number of simulations. Large differences between the top procedures and the rest are stable.

docs.title: Limits of the method
docs.text:
• The results are estimates, built on HPO annotations of diseases and MAxO annotations of procedures. If an annotation is missing, the procedure's value may be underestimated.
  • maxodiff does not consider cost, risk, invasiveness, or availability of a procedure. These are clinical decisions.
  • The analysis is limited to the diseases of the differential diagnosis. The number of diseases (20 to 40) and the number of simulations (1 to 100) can be chosen.
